flashcard_questions.a: Poor-quality housing built illegally on the steep hills around a Brazilian city.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Rio favela is one of the largest squatter settlements in South America?
What share of Rio's piped fresh water is lost before it reaches homes?
How much raw sewage pours into Guanabara Bay every day?
How high can infant mortality reach in Rio's favelas?
How low can life expectancy fall in Rio's favelas?
What percentage of Rio's children stay in school after the age of 14?
What is the unemployment rate in Rio's favelas?
How much does an informal worker in Rio earn each month?
What is the murder rate in Rio?
Why are young people in Rio's favelas drawn into gang crime?
flashcard_questions.a: Poor education and no formal work make crime the quickest way to earn.

flashcard_questions.q: How much has the number of cars in Rio risen in the last decade?
How many deaths a year does air pollution cause in Rio?
How much waste does Rio produce each year?
Why does rubbish go uncollected in Rio's favelas?
flashcard_questions.a: Narrow, steep streets stop refuse vehicles reaching the homes.

notes: 15 cards: 2 term-to-definition and place cards (favela, Complexo do Alemão), 10 case-study-to-fact with exactly one figure each (one-third of water, 200 tonnes of sewage, 50 per 1,000, 45 years, 50% staying in school, 20% unemployment, £60 a month, 20 per 1,000 murders, 40% car rise, 5,000 deaths, 3.1 million tonnes), 3 cause-to-consequence (gang crime, uncollected waste, pollution). Dropped the 55-rivers and 55%-clinic figures because the deck already carries many percentages that could interfere.
